input: This memo recommends that a three-month pilot be undertaken on 24 pumps, at a cost of $45k, before any decision is taken regarding full installation of the proposed sensor package. The plant operates a total of 180 pumps, and maintenance records covering a period of 12 months reveal no fewer than 1108 h of unplanned downtime, of which bearing failures account for a substantial 43% of the downtime hours. A sensor set covering all 180 pumps has been quoted at $426k installed, together with a recurring charge of $61k per year, and it is worth noting that in a vendor trial conducted on a comparable unit, the sensors were reported to cut downtime by 19%, although this figure originates from the vendor and has not been measured at this plant. Set against the full commitment of $426k plus $61k per year, the pilot at $45k offers a considerably lower-cost means of establishing whether the technology delivers a comparable benefit under local conditions. It should also be borne in mind that spare-part lead times are entirely unchanged by the sensors, since the sensors serve to shorten detection times rather than supply times, and a bearing that has been identified as failing will still have to await the arrival of its spare. The reliability engineering group will own the pilot and will report its findings in advance of the March capital review, and it is recommended that the decision on full installation be held until those pilot results have been reported and can be properly evaluated.
target: The recommendation is the three-month pilot on 24 pumps at $45k, before any decision on full installation. The reliability engineering group owns the pilot and reports before the March capital review. The plant runs 180 pumps. Maintenance records for 12 months show 1108 h of unplanned downtime, and bearing failures account for 43% of the downtime hours. A sensor set for all 180 pumps is quoted at $426k installed, plus $61k per year. In a vendor trial on a comparable unit, the sensors cut downtime by 19%; the figure is the vendor's and was not measured at this plant. The choice is $426k plus $61k a year for the full set, against $45k for a pilot that measures the reduction on this plant's own pumps. Bearings carry the largest single share of the downtime, so detection aimed at bearings addresses the part of the problem the records actually show. Spare-part lead times are unchanged by the sensors: detection shortens, supply does not, and a bearing caught failing still waits for its spare. The pilot therefore tests one claim, the downtime reduction, and leaves the other limit where it stands. The pilot report sets the downtime on the fitted pumps against the maintenance records for the same machines, so the vendor figure is checked on the plant's own evidence before the full price is paid. The decision on full installation is held until the pilot results are reported.
